source_note: Gutierrez-Perez & Agudo, 'Learning Human Sports Motion Feasibility via Quantile Regression on Tracking Data', arXiv:2610.36183v1 [cs.AI], 26 Oct 2026 (Marc Gutierrez-Perez, Antonio Agudo; Institut de Robotica i Informatica Industrial, CSIC-UPC, Barcelona), 17 pages; code github.com/mguti97/TTA-Quantile. Casts time-to-arrival (TTA) — shortest plausible time to reach a location given kinematic state k=(p,v,a) — as conditional lower-quantile regression at tau=0.01 (feasibility bound, lower envelope of observed locomotion, not mean/density). Eq1 tau(g)=Q0.01(Delta t|g(k,x)); Eq2 reachable-area sublevel duality R(Delta t)={x:tau(x)<=Delta t}; Eq3 pinball loss (over-prediction 99x under at tau=0.01); Eq4 differentiable area-aware sigmoid soft-count term (beta=0.25s, grid 25x25@4m |G|=624, lambda=0.01). Heading-invariant physics-normalized 6 features (d/120, cos/sin theta, v/12, ax/ay/10); self-supervised labels (~154M samples, 5 horizons [0.10,8.0]s); SUVAT noise floor discards 0.3% teleport artifacts (caps 8 m/s^2/9 m/s; ablation: noise screen not physical prior). MLP 6-64-64-1 ReLU+Softplus; profile variant + per-player max speed (99th percentile, train matches only). Benchmark vs six best-tuned physics motion models (constant speed/accel/accel+vmax/two-segment/free-direction Wu-Swartz/friction-damped Fujimura-Sugihara) inverted as TTA + Anzer-Bauer reachable-hull. Matched-coverage (99%) area comparison: MLP MAE 2.596s/area 31.6 m^2 beats all physics (two-segment 2.992/34.1) and hull (3.065/34.8), tightest 8/9 cells; profile +0.025s 95% CI [+0.019,+0.030] cluster bootstrap; representation not feature (personalized baseline trails 0.30s). Structural audit: connected/star-shaped sublevel sets 100%, monotonicity violation 1.4%. Real-time 22-player full-pitch pass 2.4ms (~420fps). Cross-sport transfer asymmetric (NFL-trained best, basketball furthest; transferred area loses to destination physics = label-regime mismatch not representation failure). Data: PFF FC FIFA World Cup 2022 (64 matches, 30fps, 45/10/9 cross-match split); NBA SportVU 2015-16 (631 games, 25fps); NFL Big Data Bowl 2019 (single game, 10fps, 729510 samples, by-player split). Extracted faithfully (not a derivative summary). Equations 1-4 printed in math font that extracts garbled; reconstructed in labeled LaTeX and flagged here and in assumptions. Domain cs matches catalog (tracking-data machine learning / quantile regression; soccer primary with basketball + NFL transfer). Directly isomorphic to GSE's arrival-time/space-control kernel, lower-quantile feasibility bound, time-area duality, teleport-artifact veto, matched-coverage tightness metric, and live-inference latency budget. No sportsbook lines/spreads/totals/implied odds in source or lifted into GSE.

primitives.name: SUVAT noise floor: discard samples faster than physically plausible (teleport artifacts)
primitives.verbatim_quote: a single teleport artifact at a given geometry can drag the predicted floor below what is physically achievable
assumptions: Because the tau=0.01 objective learns from the fastest realizations, a single teleport artifact at a given geometry can drag the predicted floor below what is physically achievable; a SUVAT closed-form kinematic intercept model (redirect phase keeping useful momentum, then sprint phase accelerating at a capped rate to a capped top speed) computes the fastest physically plausible arrival time Delta t_SUVAT for every sample, and any sample whose observed Delta t < Delta t_SUVAT is discarded along with degenerate near-zero-distance samples.

primitives.name: Filter is a noise screen, not a physical prior (removing it loosens area, not floor)

primitives.name: Eq3 pinball loss: at tau=0.01 over-prediction penalized 99x under-prediction
primitives.verbatim_quote: pushing the estimate toward the lower envelope so the model learns how quickly a player can arrive
primitives.latex: L_{\tau}(\hat y,y)=\begin{cases}\tau\,(y-\hat y) & y\ge \hat y\\ (1-\tau)(\hat y-y) & y<\hat y\end{cases},\qquad \tau=0.01
assumptions: All learned models minimize a pinball loss L_tau(yhat,y)=tau(y-yhat) for y>=yhat and (1-tau)(yhat-y) for y<yhat, augmented with an area-aware auxiliary term; at tau=0.01 over-prediction is penalized 99 times more heavily than under-prediction, pushing the estimate toward the lower envelope so the model learns how quickly a player can arrive. reasoning_traces.think: The retrocausal genealogy of this paper is the arrival-time turn in player-motion modeling. Marc Gutierrez-Perez and Antonio Agudo of the Institut de Robotica i Informatica Industrial in Barcelona, posting to arXiv in October 2026 as 2610.36183, argue that space is the currency of team sports and that almost every pitch-control, off-ball-value, or pass-probability surface rests on a player-motion model answering where a player can get to and how fast. The work sits between two dominant strands: the closed-form physical motion models of Taki and Hasegawa, Fujimura and Sugihara, Renkin, Wu and Swartz, and Narizuka, which are interpretable and parameter-light but commit to a fixed functional form, and the data-driven space models of Fernandez and Bornn, Brefeld, Spencer, and Wu, which are flexible but discard physically meaningful arrival time in favor of a density or behavioral-commitment probability. The paper's contribution is to keep the interpretable output type of the motion-model literature, an arrival time invertible to a reachable area, while inheriting the accuracy of a data-driven regressor, building on Koenker and Bassett's regression quantiles and Anzer and Bauer's expected-passes reachable hulls. The recursive theory of mind is the lower-quantile feasibility formulation and its geometric duality. The quantity of interest is the minimum time-to-arrival from a kinematic state of position, velocity, and acceleration to any target location, framed as conditional quantile regression at the first percentile because the target is a feasibility bound — the player could be there in time — rather than a typical-case estimate; a player may dawdle anywhere so the upper tail is uninformative, but the floor on how quickly they can plausibly arrive is sharply defined. A single observed trajectory only upper-bounds what the player could have done, but across roughly 154 million extracted samples many share a kinematic state with the player fully committed, so the pinball loss at the first percentile recovers the fast tail and discards choice-driven slowness. The reachable area is exactly the sublevel set of the arrival-time surface, a duality that lets a time output be evaluated with an area metric. Cross-layer veto adjudication is the matched-coverage benchmark and its ablations. The model is a small multilayer perceptron with a Softplus output whose linear growth extrapolates gracefully beyond the training horizon, trained on six physics-normalized heading-invariant features with a per-player max-speed capacity feature added in the profile variant, and optimized with a pinball loss that penalizes over-prediction ninety-nine times more than under-prediction plus a differentiable area-aware sigmoid soft-count term. A SUVAT noise floor discards the 0.3 percent of samples faster than physically plausible, and the ablation shows this is a noise screen rather than a physical prior because removing it leaves the floor unchanged while loosening areas and raising monotonicity violations from 1.4 to 23.4 percent of rays. Both quantile MLPs beat every physics baseline and the learned reachable-hull baseline on point error and pinball, and are tightest in eight of nine matched-coverage cells, with the profile advantage confirmed by a paired cluster bootstrap whose confidence interval excludes zero. The implementation invariants map directly onto GSE. The conditional first-percentile arrival-time regression is GSE's lower-quantile feasibility kernel underlying safe-pass targeting and pass-probability surfaces; the sublevel-set duality is GSE's invertible arrival-time-to-reachable-region bridge; the heading-invariant physics-normalized features are GSE's cross-context motion representation; the SUVAT plausibility screen is GSE's teleport-artifact veto on training labels; the matched-coverage area comparison is GSE's precision-at-fixed-recall tightness metric; and the real-time full-pitch forward pass at 2.4 milliseconds is GSE's live-deployment latency budget. The structural audit confirming connected, star-shaped sublevel sets with negligible monotonicity violation is GSE's geometric-validity verification for learned space surfaces. The cross-sport transfer results make the portability boundary concrete and honest. Retrained unchanged on basketball and American-football tracking, each sport's own model beats that sport's two-segment baseline in-domain, confirming the recipe is not tuned to one geometry; but transfer is markedly asymmetric, with the American-football-trained checkpoint transferring out essentially for free on point error and pinball while basketball's slower, more lateral game sits furthest in kinematic regime. Crucially, every transferred checkpoint's reachable area loses to the destination's own physics baseline even where its point error wins, a mismatch traced to label regime — American-football pass plays are short, explosive, straight-line sprints with faster arrival times at matched distance and speed — rather than to a failure of the representation. The caveats close the account with the scope limits that bound the claim. The heading invariance deliberately discards absolute pitch position and boundary context, buying cross-sport portability at the cost of sideline and end-zone awareness; the per-player max-speed feature is estimated only from training matches to avoid leakage; and the authors are explicit that a fixed closed-form motion model is not necessary to produce a physically plausible, well-calibrated reachable-area estimate, while noting that richer personalization and transfer across leagues and tracking providers within soccer remain future work. The invariant for GSE is to adopt the lower-quantile feasibility formulation, the time-area sublevel duality, the physics-normalized heading-invariant representation, the SUVAT noise screen, the matched-coverage tightness metric, the area-aware regularizer, and the real-time inference budget, while carrying the boundary-context discard, the label-regime transfer asymmetry, and the representation-versus-feature attribution as honest bounds on what a learned locomotion model can claim across sports.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: Arrival-time turn in player-motion modeling. Marc Gutierrez-Perez, Antonio Agudo (IRI CSIC-UPC Barcelona); arXiv:2610.36183v1 [cs.AI] 26 Oct 2026; GitHub mguti97/TTA-Quantile. Space=currency; pitch-control/off-ball/pass-prob all rest on motion model. Between closed-form physics (Taki-Hasegawa 2000, Fujimura-Sugihara 2005, Renkin 2022, Wu-Swartz 2025, Narizuka 2023) and data-driven space (Fernandez-Bornn 2018, Brefeld 2019, Spencer 2019, Wu 2022) which discard arrival time for density. Keeps interpretable arrival-time output (invertible to reachable area) + data-driven accuracy. Builds on Koenker-Bassett 1978 regression quantiles, Anzer-Bauer 2022 expected passes reachable hulls, Spearman 2017/2018 time-to-intercept, Schilling 2026 safe passing regions NFL, Augustine 2025 NFL pass completion, Yurko 2020 going-deep.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: TTA = min plausible arrival time from k=(p,v,a) to target x; conditional quantile regression Eq1 tau(g)=Q0.01(Delta t|g(k,x)) (feasibility bound not typical case; upper tail uninformative/dawdle, floor sharp). Single trajectory only upper-bounds; ~154M samples share committed kinematic state; pinball@1st percentile recovers fast tail, discards choice-driven slowness. Eq2 duality R(Delta t)={x:tau(x)<=Delta t}, invert tau(x)=min{t:x in R(t)}. Heading frame (translate origin + rotate -phi, lateral v drops); 6 features d/120,cos/sin theta,v/12,ax/ay/10 (physics-normalized, cross-sport portable); angle (cos,sin) avoids 2pi discontinuity; discards boundary context. Self-supervised labels (own future arrival, 5 horizons [0.10,8.0]s). SUVAT noise floor (redirect+sprint, caps 8 m/s^2/9 m/s) discards observed<SUVAT (0.3%). MLP 6-64-64-1 ReLU+Softplus (linear extrapolation); profile +per-player vmax (99th pct, 45 train matches). Eq3 pinball tau=0.01 over-pred 99x under; Eq4 L_area=mean sigmoid((h-tauhat)/beta) beta=0.25 grid 25x25@4m |G|=624 h{3,5}; L=L_tau+0.01 L_area. Eqs 1-4 math-font reconstructed.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Benchmark: 6 physics models inverted + reachable-hull, fit by reachable-area score (best-tuned). Coverage=fraction trails tau_pred(xt)<=Delta t; area=sublevel pitch area; coverage 1.0 trivial by whole-pitch inflation -> never rank alone; matched coverage 99%, smallest area=tighter, horizons {1..5}s. MLP MAE 2.596+/-0.005/RMSE 3.193/pinball 0.028/area 31.6; profile 2.577/31.7; two-segment 2.992/34.1; friction 2.984/35.0; hull 3.065/34.8; tightest 8/9 cells. Data-driven alone != tight envelope (quantile formulation is). Profile vs base +0.025s 95% CI [+0.019,+0.030] paired cluster bootstrap 9 matches; personalized baseline still trails 0.30s -> representation not feature. SUVAT filter off -> floor unchanged, area +31%/12-17%, monotonicity 1.4%->23.4% (noise screen not prior). Structural audit: connected+star-shaped 100% (25000 cases/80000 rays), monotonicity violation 1.4% (tau>4s,>20m,16ms). Real-time 22-player 157080-row pass 2.4ms ~420fps RTX A5000. Cross-sport asymmetric: NFL-trained transfers best, basketball furthest; transferred area loses to destination physics (label-regime mismatch: NFL short explosive straight-line sprints) not representation failure. Data PFF FC WC2022 64 matches 30fps 45/10/9; NBA SportVU 2015-16 631 games 25fps; NFL BDB 2019 single game 10fps 729510 samples by-player. Boundary context discarded; closed-form not necessary. Zero sportsbook lines lifted.

universal_lens: A lower-quantile regression treatment of player motion feasibility estimates time-to-arrival as the conditional first percentile of observed locomotion — a sharply defined feasibility floor rather than an uninformative mean or a density — over physics-normalized heading-invariant geometry, with a reachable-area sublevel duality, an asymmetric pinball loss, a differentiable area-aware regularizer, and a SUVAT teleport-artifact noise screen; a compact MLP beats six best-tuned closed-form motion models and a learned reachable-hull baseline on point error and matched-coverage area, transfers asymmetrically across soccer, basketball, and American football with a label-regime rather than representation mismatch, and runs a full 22-player pitch-control map in 2.4 milliseconds, showing that a fixed closed-form motion model is not necessary for a physically plausible, well-calibrated reachable-area estimate.

gse_mapping: GSE lifts the conditional first-percentile arrival-time regression as its lower-quantile feasibility kernel for safe-pass targeting and pass-probability surfaces, the time-area sublevel duality as its invertible arrival-time-to-reachable-region bridge, the physics-normalized heading-invariant representation as its cross-context motion features, the SUVAT plausibility screen as its teleport-artifact veto on training labels, the matched-coverage smallest-area comparison as its precision-at-fixed-recall tightness metric, the asymmetric pinball plus area-aware regularizer as its lower-envelope objective, the per-player max-speed conditioning as its personalized athletic-ceiling input, the structural connected/star-shaped audit as its geometric-validity verification, and the 2.4ms full-pitch forward pass as its live-deployment latency budget; treats the boundary-context discard, the cross-sport label-regime transfer asymmetry (point error transfers but reachable area loses to destination physics), and the representation-versus-feature attribution as honest bounds, and the finding that a fixed closed-form motion model is unnecessary for a calibrated reachable-area estimate as license for its learned space surfaces; all outputs are arrival-time and reachability estimates from tracking data, never sportsbook lines.
